# Ruby 1.8.7-p374, vendored for vkxp

This directory is a subset of the Ruby 1.8.7 patch level 374 release, kept at its original
relative paths. `vkxp-ruby-sys` compiles it into the interpreter that runs game scripts.

## Origin

- Release: `ruby-1.8.7-p374.tar.gz`, from
  `https://cache.ruby-lang.org/pub/ruby/1.8/ruby-1.8.7-p374.tar.gz`
- SHA-256 of the tarball:
  `876eeeaaeeab10cbf4767833547d66d86d6717ef48fd3d89e27db8926a65276c`

`MANIFEST.sha256` lists the upstream SHA-256 of every vendored file, in the format of
`sha256sum`. `PATCHES.md` lists every local change, and `patches/` holds the diffs. A test in
`vkxp-ruby-sys` checks the tree against both: no file may be added, removed or changed without
a record. The four files that vkxp adds (`MANIFEST.sha256`, `PATCHES.md`, `README.vkxp.md` and
the contents of `patches/`) are not part of the release.

## Licence

The MIT licence of the vkxp repository does not cover this directory. Ruby is under the Ruby
licence or the GPL version 2, at the user's choice: see `COPYING` (`COPYING.ja` in Japanese) and
`GPL`. Some files have their own terms, listed in `LEGAL`; of the vendored ones, `regex.c` and
`regex.h` are under the LGPL (`LGPL`), and `parse.c`, `st.c`, `st.h`, `util.c` and `random.c`
have the terms that `LEGAL` gives for them. `README` is the release's own. `regex.c` and
`regex.h` are kept as the release has them but are not built or included: the regular
expression engine is Oniguruma, in `third_party/oniguruma-5.9.6/` under its own licence.

## How the subset was chosen

The release has 2585 files; about 160 are kept, in four groups.

- **To build the interpreter.** The 38 C files that the release's own build puts into
  `libruby-static.a` (`array bignum class compar dir dln enum enumerator error eval file gc hash
  inits io marshal math numeric object pack parse process prec random range re regex ruby signal
  sprintf st string struct time util variable version dmyext`), of which vkxp builds all but
  `regex` (see `PATCHES.md`, patch 13), `lex.c` (included by `parse.c`),
  the headers they include (`defines.h dln.h env.h intern.h missing.h node.h regex.h re.h ruby.h
  rubyio.h rubysig.h st.h util.h version.h`) and the `Zlib` binding `ext/zlib/zlib.c`. `parse.c`
  and `lex.c` are shipped pre-generated by the release. `config.h`, the one file `configure`
  would generate, lives in `crates/vkxp-ruby-sys/config/` per target. The patched `parse.c`
  includes `vkxp_symbol_table.h`, which the build script of `vkxp-ruby-sys` generates from
  `crates/vkxp-ruby-sys/data/symbols.startup.txt` (see `PATCHES.md`, patch 11). The patched
  `re.h` and `parse.c` include `vkxp_regex.h` from `crates/vkxp-ruby-sys/compat/`, which leads
  to the headers of the vendored Oniguruma (patch 14).
- **To run Ruby's own tests.** `main.c`, `ext/fcntl/fcntl.c`, `ext/stringio/stringio.c` and
  `ext/purelib.rb` for the test executable; `test/runner.rb`, `test/ruby/`,
  `test/zlib/test_zlib.rb` and `sample/test.rb` as the suites; `lib/test/` and
  `lib/{delegate,fileutils,generator,optparse,tempfile,timeout,tmpdir}.rb` as the libraries the
  suites load. None of these is part of the interpreter that vkxp ships.
- **For provenance.** `parse.y` and `keywords`, the sources of `parse.c` and `lex.c`.
- **Licence.** `COPYING`, `COPYING.ja`, `GPL`, `LGPL`, `LEGAL`, `README`.

Everything else (the standard library, the other extensions, documentation, the `configure`
machinery, the Windows and other platform ports) is left out: the original runtime exposes only
the core library and `Zlib`.
